result.title: DiA: Directional Adapter
result.comment: Accepted at NeurIPS 2026. Joint first authors with equal contributions. Code - https://github.com/prakashchhipa/DiA-Directional-Adapter
result.summary: Fine-grained action recognition often depends on how an action unfolds over time rather than on appearance alone. Visually similar classes may differ in preparation, execution, or completion phases, making uniformly aggregated temporal context suboptimal. We study this problem under a practical objective: i) improving recognition performance with few tunable parameters, ii) being compute efficient, and iii) using only the readily available video modality. Motivated by this missing temporal observation and the accuracy--compute efficiency--unimodality objective, we propose Directional Adapter (DiA), a parameter-efficient adapter on top of CLIP. DiA formulates temporal specialization into causal and anti-causal directions, allowing past-to-present and future-to-present cues to be modeled differently. To keep this directional modeling parameter- and compute-efficient, both directions use depth-wise temporal convolutions in a compact bottleneck space and are combined through a learnable fusion. DiA achieves state-of-the-art performance among methods using a single video input modality across seven public benchmarks, with only $\sim$3.6M tunable parameters, while also delivering higher throughput and lower inference latency than prior methods. Code is available at https://github.com/prakashchhipa/DiA-Directional-Adapter.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 DiA：在 CLIP 上加入参数高效的方向性适配器，把时序建模分为因果与反因果两个方向，用瓶颈空间中的深度可分离时序卷积分别捕捉「过去→现在」与「未来→现在」线索，并以可学习融合组合，在单一视频模态下提升细粒度动作识别。
AI.relevance_reason: 其因果/反因果双方向建模与可学习融合，可能为 latent 推理状态如何分别整合既定历史与前瞻证据、并在紧凑瓶颈空间中低成本更新提供架构线索；但原文面向动作识别分类、不涉及 VLM 推理，迁移可行性需核查。
